title: Lord, in Whose Might the Saviour Trod
description: Lord, in Whose Might the Saviour Trod in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 117, “Christ Walking on the Sea”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, in whose might the Sa-viour trod The dark and storm-y wave, And trust-ed in his Fa-ther's arm, Om-ni-po-tent to save;

lines: Lord, in whose might the Saviour trod
And trusted in his Father's arm,
When darkly round our footsteps rise
The floods and storms of life,
Send Thou Thy Spirit down to still
Strong in our trust, on Thee reposed,
Though waves around us rage and foam,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch died in 1870.
credits: Words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
